That covers the boundary and error situations across saving, finding, and the read-later views. I think we've reached a complete, coherent picture for a first version.

Here's everything that's settled so far — in plain terms:

**Saving a link**
- Paste an address and the title, description, site icon, and preview image fill in automatically; you can edit the title/description before saving.
- Only the link is required; you can add tags (with suggestions from tags you've used before) and a private note.
- If a link can't be read, you can still save it and fill in the details yourself; if it isn't a real web address, you're asked to fix it.
- Saving the same link twice never makes a duplicate — you're taken to the existing one to update it (including when you edit a link to match another).

**Finding a link again**
- One search box looks across title, description, note, tags, and address at once, live as you type, ignoring capitalization, with matches highlighted and a match count.
- Powerful searches: exact tag with `#tag`, combining words, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` with parentheses, and `"exact phrases"`.
- Click any tag to filter by it; note-only matches show a highlighted excerpt so you know why they appeared.

**Read later vs. finished**
- Choose "save to read later" (on by default) or save as a reference.
- All / To read / Finished tabs with counts; mark items finished or move them back — nothing is ever deleted, and finished items stay searchable.

**When things aren't tidy**
- Friendly messages for empty lists and no-results; long content wraps neatly.

A couple of things we agreed to leave for **later versions** (I've noted them): automatic dead-link detection, and general look-and-feel polish.

**May I now move on to building this as the real application?** Once you approve, I'll switch from exploring to implementing this scope.
